overview: AI‑enabled ransomware attacks are rising, leveraging LLMs for phishing and negotiation.
Nvidia’s leadership turmoil highlights security and export‑control risks in the global AI chip market.
Google launches Gemini‑powered smart glasses, emphasizing privacy features amid renewed wearables interest.

top.title: Beware the New AI-Fueled Ransomware Boom
top.summary: Ransomware incidents have surged 20‑40% this summer, with AI tools aiding phishing and negotiation, raising concerns about future fully AI‑driven extortion.

top.title: Jensen Huang is out. What did China want from him?
top.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned amid allegations of a Chinese spy relationship, sparking debate over China’s motives and US‑China AI tensions.

top.title: Google pushes privacy angle as Gemini-powered smartglasses debut starting at $395
top.summary: Google, Samsung, and designers released Gemini‑enabled smart glasses starting at $395, featuring voice AI, open‑ear speakers, and privacy‑focused microphones.

top.title: Where was Nvidia’s security team?
top.summary: Nvidia’s long‑time CSO left for health reasons; his successor’s knowledge of the Megaspeed probe is unclear, highlighting corporate security gaps.

top.title: Asian governments react to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s exit
top.summary: Asian governments responded to Huang’s exit, confirming chip supply commitments while monitoring export‑control impacts on Chinese AI projects.

top.title: The OpenAI board member who fired Sam Altman says we still can’t trust AI CEOs
top.summary: Former OpenAI board member Helen Toner warns that reliance on individual CEOs for AI safety is flawed, urging stronger governance structures.
